findings.basis: Rule round 62, item 1, a close part. T-Mobile 310-240 and 310-260, 17 bundles. On 3, fi_tmo_us and u264a_us, the read stood against Google's own false. On 14, tracfonetmo_us, consumercellulartmo_us, redpockettmo_us and one GID entry, the own entry sets the main key true and leaves this key unset on every row read. That silence may only be lag, and a hold follows Google either way. A read cannot part the 3 from the 14. All tmobile_us SIMs keep true from the lane.
findings.effect: Android's default is false (CarrierConfigManager.java:10991-10992,12197). ImsRegistrationTracker.isRttSupported (:585-598) and AosCondition::IsRttSupported (:999-1011) read it after the main key, so it does nothing while rtt_supported_bool is off. On a SIM with RTT on, true adds TEXT to the normal REGISTER while roaming and stops the native TTY deregistration; false leaves both as on any SIM with RTT off. Nothing on the emergency path reads this key (AosHandleEmergencyMtc.cpp:56 reads the main key only). Telephony's readers sit behind config_support_rtt, which is false. Read, not tested.
findings.risk: No harm was found. From holding, these SIMs follow Google's own entry both ways. Nothing here says what the network does.
